speaker: Isabel Miller
words: I'm Isabel Miller and I'm here on the 22nd of March to talk to Peggy Egland. Now, the first thing we do is fill out a personal data sheet. We usually do it while we are recording. We were interviewing your mother and your sister this morning. What is your maiden name?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Boyer.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Is it Margaret or just Peggy?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Just Peggy.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: And you don't have any other nicknames?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: No.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: When were you born?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: December 23, 1951.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: And where were you born?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Hawthorne, California.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: And what is your address here?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Route 1, Genesee.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: What was your first residence in Idaho?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Nez Perce.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: And you came directly there from California?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Well, my folks moved [unintelligible] and went to Cali fornia for the winter.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: And that's how you happened to be born down there? Then, when you were less than a year old, you came back up here and that would have been 1952?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yes.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Did they travel by car, then?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yes, I think they came by car.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: And it was your whole family?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yes.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: What is your mother's maiden name?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Johnson.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Her first name?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Jeanette.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Do you know her birthday?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: March 19. I don't know the year.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Do you know where she was born?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: I'm sure in Nez Perce. I don't know.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Do you know what year she was married?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: No.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Did she have any jobs or occupations?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: I don't think so.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: She was just a homemaker?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yes.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: What is your father's name?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Robert.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Do you know when he was born?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: No, I don't even know his birthday.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: What kinds of jobs did he have?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: He's a farmer.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: And he's always done that?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yes.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Do you know where he was born?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: In Nez Perce, I think.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: And both your father and mother are living?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yes.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Do you have any sisters?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: I have two sisters.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: And what are their names?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Donna, and Phyllis who is married, her name is Kuther.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: And Donna's not married?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: No.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Do you have brothers?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yes.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Their names?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Randy, Steve, Keith, Larry and Stan.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Are they younger than you?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: They're all younger.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: They're all younger and you are the oldest. Your husband's name is?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Nick.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: And he's a student now. Has he had any jobs?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: He was in the army.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: And I've got his birthday and everything on the other sheet, so I can transfer it to here. Where were you married?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: In Moscow.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: What date were you married?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: October 21, 1972.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: And no children. How much education did you have?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: I'm still in school.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Oh, you're still a student at the University?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yes, I'm going to graduate this spring.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: What is your major?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Pre-vet.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Do you have any other skills and things you like to do?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: I like to sew.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: And jobs?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: I was a swimming instructor last summer.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: What other jobs have you held?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: I drove a grain truck.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Do you have any other interests or hobbies or anything that you like to do?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: I did a little bit of water color painting.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Do you have any clubs or groups or organizations that you are a member of?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: I'm a member of Alpha Zeta and that's all.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Have you done Four-H work?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yeah, I was with Four-H for some time .

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Did you get awards, honors or ribbons in there? Quite a few?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yes.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: About how many years?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: I believ~ for eight years.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Did you exhibit and raise animals mostly?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yeah, sewing and animals.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Okay, that's personal data about you. Then we have some questions. These are mostly about how you've made decisions in your life and how you got to the place where you are now. What you project your future to be. Mostly the are just to stimulate you to think about and go into some other areas. So, if there's anything that reminds you of, and you want to talk about, well, we want you to do that, too. Do you see advantages in living in rural areas?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yes, I think so.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Do you know anybody that lives in urban areas that you could compare your life to?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: I don't know very many people.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: But you see this life as having more advantages over other people?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yeah. When Nick was in the army, we lived in a ... it wasn't a large town, but I liked it a lot better.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: You began to appreciate what you had from personal experience?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yes.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Most people say how it's a better place to raise children. Do you agree with that?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yes, I would.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: And, of course, if you are interested in being a veterinar ian, that's where the opportunity and the jobs are.

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yeah.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Do you plan to be a vet in a rural area that would be with animals, or do you think small animals, or would you use your business for both?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: I'd like it to be both.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: So one supplements the other.

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yes.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Are there any other ways you might compare a rural woman and an urban woman? Were there things you missed being in that area?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Well, because I like animals I think that's on thing. You can have dogs and cats and raise meat and if you like animals, that's one thing. Begin away from people, not having neighbors upstairs and downstairs and to your right and to your left.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: That was restrictive for you?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Uh huh. I think it's pretty out in the country because you have trees and the country is prettier.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: What did you do while your husband was in the army? How did you spend your days?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Well, at first I tried to find a job. I didn't want to work as a waitress or something like that, that I didn't enjoy. I ended up not finding a job and I didn't do much of anything. We didn't know very many people there; it was hard to get to know anybody. I just sewed and we had a dog. That's about all I did.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: How long was this period?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: From October to May.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: He got out of the army and then you came right back?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yeah, I came back and worked for my dad and then he got out and he [unintelligible].

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Where was he located?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Fort Leavenworth.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: You lived right in the town of Leavenworth?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yes.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Of course, you don't have any children of your own yet, but anticipate that you'll raise your children about the same as the way you grew up?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: I think so, yeah.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: You feel pretty satisfied with the way your family raised you, the things you did?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yes.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: You wouldn't want to make any changes?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: No, I don't think so.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Your father was a farmer and you grew up on the farm? Did the boys and girls help with the chores?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Well, we didn't have any animals. We just raised wheat. Well, one of the first animals we had, I decided I wanted to go into Four-H. So I went out and got a lamb and then we tried to get some sheep and raise sheep steers. But, that's all the animals we had.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: So, there wasn't really a lot of jobs because you were on a farm, that were different than, say, maybe in town?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: No.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Did you have the housework at home? You helped your mother?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yes.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Were the boys expected to help, then?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: We all had to do the dishes every night and we all had a little chore to do after dinner; but, that's about all we had to do.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Was there yardwork for the boys to do?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yeah, not very much.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Just in the summer time?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yes.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Was there anything that you thought you could not do because you were a girl?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: I can't think of anything that I wanted to do then that I couldn't do. We started a track team and a basketball team, but we didn't have very many coaches. Not that I wanted to be a basketball player or anything like that, but because I was a girl you didn't have that training that boys get.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: You just didn't have the opportunities developed as you were growing up and mostly the girls did it on their own if they wanted to, so there was no real encouragement.

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yeah.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: How about facilities, did you have time in the gym?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yeah, we had all that. But the main thing was getting a coach that knew anything about it.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: When you decided to go to college, was it your decision or your parents?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: I don't know what I wanted to do. Dad wanted me to go on and get an education. I knew I didn't want to stay home and just work. I just wanted to go to college a year and figure out what I wanted to do. Dad wanted me to go to [unintelligible) and I'd have to go to Pocatello. But I didn't want to go that far, so I came up here. Meanwhile, I got interested in pre-vet.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: So, there was no feeling that because you were a. girl you didn't need schooling? They felt that you needed it just as much as ...

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: No. Dad expected me to go to school.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Were you expected to get married?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: No.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: That was your decision to make, too?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yeah. Dad wanted me to get an education so that if I got married or didn't get married and if anything happened in my life, I'd have the education behind me.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Did you get married sooner than they wanted you to? Would they prefer that you graduated first?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: I don't think they cared that I got married. I think it bothered them that I quit school to get married.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: They were afraid you wouldn't go back?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yeah.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: So, they are more at ease now that you are finishing school?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yeah.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Where did you meet your husband?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: At school.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: You had dating and the usual courtship there before you got married?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yeah.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: About how long did you go together before you were married?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: A year and a half, I think.

speaker: NE
words: We knew each other for a year and a half.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: And you got married about the time he went in the army?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: No, he'd already been in about six months. He came home on leave during the summer; then we decided to get married.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: You just got married because you wanted to?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yes.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Like, for some women, it's a way to make a living. But, for you, you just decided you wanted to be with him?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: We had planned to wait until later, but I don't know.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: You decided not to wait.

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yeah.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: So far, of course it's not been very long, but has your expectations of marriage been what you thought?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yeah, I think so.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Have you made any decisions about how many children you want or how soon you'll have them or anything like that?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: No. I don't want to have a large family. As far as that, I want to have a place, you know, a place to call our home. And I'd like to have a job and have enough money, just be a little more settled.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: What do you mean by large? What would be the ideal family?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Probably three.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Your father had a wheat farm, so the children weren't helping out that much. Do you think your parents wanted eight children?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: I don't know.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: There was a time in pioneer days when they made children helpers and workers on a farm. But it wasn't that way in your family?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: I don't think so. I think they just had that many. Like, Dad didn't have too much money then, and it was kind of hard for him to finally get where he was with so many children. So, I think it was just the thing to do was have a big family.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: They just kind of came along. What did your family do for recreation?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: I don't know.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Well, Four-H might be counted as one of your activities. What did your mother and father do? Did you ever do things together as a family, like camping or anything like that?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Well, picnicking was about it. We never did that much together.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: There was a wide age range from you, the oldest. How young is the youngest one?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Steve is eight, I think.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: So there's probably not a lot of things that you could do that everybody would be interested in. Did you have television at home?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Oh, yeah.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Do you remember what magazines you would read at home? Did your parents take magazines?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yeah, I don't remember the magazines at all.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Do you remember any particular programs that were a favorite?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Not really.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: You, right now, do you and your husband have a program that you watch together?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: We watch TV all the time. I don't know. I like "The Waltons,'' but Nick doesn't like it.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Is it important to see the news regularly?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yeah, we always watch the news.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Do you get educational TV here?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: No, we only get one channel.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: So, you are pretty limited to what's on then, aren't you? What do you and Nick do now for recreation? Do you have friends in?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: I guess that's what we do. People come over and party a little bit.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Do you both drive into campus in the morning and just stay all day?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yes.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: And you both come home together?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yes.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: It's like going to a job for both of you?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yeah.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Do you ever do anything with Nick's family as far as recre ation?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yeah, we go over there.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: On Sundays or for meals?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Well ...

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Whenever you feel like it?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yeah.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: I asked you about your job. Was there ever a time when your mother supported the family? Do you think she ever worried about what she would do if something happened to your father?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: I'm sure, yeah.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: If anything happened to Nick, would you be able to make a living for yourself? Have you thought about that?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Well, I would go to medical technology school next year. If something happened to Nick, I think I could get the money to go to school from my dad, and if I get this degree then I'll be able to get a job.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: In the vet program is there any differences in opportunities for women rather than for men?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: I don't think so. I think the women have as good of an opportunity or better than the men do.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Is that with small animals?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: I think with both. If they want to work with large animals and be permanent enough to get in, then I think the opportunities are the same.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: There's really no prejudice against you, say, in a farm community?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: There might be, I don't know.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: So far, you haven't gotten that far. Does it worry you, does that bother you?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: No.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Do you and Nick plan to work together and have kind of a partnership?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: I don't know.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: You'll just wait and see what kind of opportunities you have?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yeah.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Would you like to settle in this area in northern Idaho?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yeah. I don't know where I'd like it the best. I like it, not right here in Genesee, but like Coeur d'Alene and that area around there.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Would you consider going as far away as Washington or Oregon or Utah if you had an opportunity?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yes.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: That wouldn't bother you at all?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: No.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: So, you're really open to some options. Do you anticipate differences with your married life from, say, your parents' married life?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yes, quite a bit. Nick and I are pretty equal, like we're both going to school and we both help with the housework. In my parents' home, my dad was always out and away from the home. Morn was always at home and having children, that's another thing. As soon as my folks got married they just started having kids which was the thing to be doing. Right now, Nick and I want to wait until we are really ready and we have enough money.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: That is a big difference, isn't it?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yes.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: And I heard you say when the decisions about your future or having a job, you said, "My father wanted me to." Is it signifi cant to say where your mother was on that?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: I don't know where she was on it.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: You just don't have any impression of any strong feelings from her?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: No, I'm sure that she was as concerned about me going to school as Dad was. But, Dad was the one that made the point.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Did you have the feeling that he made decisions about how money was spent more than your mother?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yeah, I think so.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Do you have the feeling that he made most of the decisions in the family? Or did your mother share them?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: I think he made most of the decisions?

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: And you don't really anticipate you're going to have an equal say or talk it over more?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yeah, I think we'll be equal in making decisions.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: When you do decide to move or something, it's going to be both of you finding something to do?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Maybe and maybe not.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: It's not possible that Nick has priority?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: No. Like, if he gets a really good opportunity someplace, then we'll go there. But if I get a really good opportunity there, depending on what the other one is doing.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: So that you see that the other one is able to find something to do. It's not going to be either or, but whoever has one, the best opportunity. And you've thought something in preparing if something happened to Nick, you're not going to be absolutely dependent on him for your income. Do you go to church?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: No, we don't go to church.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: So there's no community activities that you're both in?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: No.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Most of your time is spent in school?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yes.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: And you did say that you placed things in county fairs and got ribbons for that?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yes.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: This is kind of a different question, but the questions is: Having observed your family and grown up on a farm, if you had a friend who was going to marry a farmer now and she hadn't had any experience, what do you think she'd need to know? What kind of adjustment would she have to make on a farm?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Well, I think she'd have to be able to appreciate the things you have on a farm, like now, I like animals. She should be able to appreciate the things you have on a farm that you don't have in a large town. Like, if she moved out to the farm and she expected it to be the same as in the city, she wouldn't have any thing to do.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: So, it is different as she would have to develop some other interests, maybe, if she didn't already have them?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yes, I think so.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: You've made some big decisions already after you got out of the army -- what you were going to do next. Did you both talk about that and decide?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Well, I think before we even got married we planned on going back to school when he got out.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: You talked about all those things even before you got married? So, you knew pretty much what your goals were for three or four years?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yes.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Are there things now that you make decisions about and things he mades decisions about? Is your life pretty close?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: It's pretty close, like I keep the house down and he makes sure the car runs. Other than that, most of the decisions, we both make them.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Now, when you come home from the campus, do you stop some where and decide what you're going to have for supper together?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: No.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Who does that?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: I don't know. I usually put out some meat in the morning and when I get home I start putting it on and he usually cooks and helps. But this year, he doesn't have classes on Tuesday and Thursday, he doesn't even have to go to school. So he fixes dinner on those days.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: It's ready when you get home; that must be nice. And you both, I assume, you both like rural life?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yes.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Is there anything by now that you would change that you would have done differently?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: I don't think so.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Was there a time when he was in the army that you might have wished that you stayed in school?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yeah, I wished I was doing something.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: So, it was not a very good time for you because you couldn't find a job that you wanted?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yeah, I didn't like it.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: But, at least you knew it was going to end sometime.

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yeah.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Can you think of any questions that you'd like to ask that I haven't?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: No.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: It makes a difference what questions you ask. Like, with your grandmother, she's been married for 50 something years. It takes longer to get through the questions. I guess we'd like to give you an opportunity to say how you feel about things. Are you comfortable with the idea of not being dependent on Nick, say, as contrasted to your mother?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yes, I feel a lot better. After we were married, I sort of depended on him because when we didn't have any friends, I was just hanging on him to take me out and play tennis and entertain me. But now, I feel a lot better because I can go out and do this.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Were you living in an area where there were not other army wives?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Well, there were army wives, but I'm not real friendly. I didn't get along with them.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: There were differences, then?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: There were differences. Most of them had gotten married pretty young and most of them had small children and we really didn't have very much in common.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: So, somehow all the contacts from outside were from Nick?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yes.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: And really, the idea of being dependent on him filled most of your needs?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yes.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Arn I right in saying that you wouldn't let that situation develop again?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Right.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Well, I think that it has been very interesting to talk to you. Can you think of anything else then? How do you feel about the women's movement? Have you met anybody at the Univer sity that is much involved in that?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: No, not really. I think in college women have equal oppor tunities as men do, and in jobs they have equal opportunities. But, I think back in grade school and high school, they don't and they need to have more activities for girls.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: When you first started to make the decision to come to college, did you decide what work you were going into?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: No.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: You were just going to try out things?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yes. I wanted to get away from home and I wanted to ... I didn't think I was smart enough to go to college. But, I thought if maybe I went to college for a year, maybe I would look at things differently, you know, what I wanted to do.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: So, you really felt like you had to get away from home and try out some other things?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yes.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Did you have tests or anything like that in high school that could tell anything?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Well, I was an honor student and I knew everything that I didn't want to do, but I couldn't think positive of what I wanted to do. I didn't want to nurse and I didn't wnt to go into business and I didn't know what I wanted.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: How did you get directed?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: In college you have to put in a major, so I put down biology because I like that. I went to summer school and I got pretty good grades, so then I thought that I could do whatever I wanted. So, I went up and talked to Dr. [unintelli gible] and then I decided I wanted to go into vet.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: He must have been encouraging.

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yes, he was.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: That makes a difference.

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yeah.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Well, I think that covers it pretty well. I guess one other thing was when you graduated from high school -- did the boys in your class seem like they knew what they were doing, if you kept track of anybody in the high school class?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: I don't think so. There was only one that I think really knew what he wanted to do and everybody else kind of knew what field they wanted to get into.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Did you have counselors in school?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Not really. Nobody talked to us about careers and stuff like that.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: You were pretty much on your own and whatever parents' help you could get? ----------------------- ---------· ---- - ---· ---~-

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yeah.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Have you thought of anything else you'd like to say?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: No.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: You seem to be working toward your goals now. How long will it be before Nick is a graduate?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: A year come this May.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: So, you're going to add medical technology next year because you are just going to be here next year?

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Yes.

speaker: Isabel Miller
words: Well, that sounds like good planning.

speaker: Peggy Egland
words: Really.
